name: How do I make a small primary bathroom feel larger?

mainEntity.name: What design choices make a small primary bathroom feel bigger without expanding the footprint?
mainEntity.text: What design choices make a small primary bathroom feel bigger without expanding the footprint?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best way to make a small primary bathroom feel larger is to reduce visual barriers and improve light. A frameless glass shower enclosure helps the room read as one continuous space instead of several chopped-up zones. Lighter tile, simpler cabinet fronts, larger mirrors, and strong layered lighting can all make the room feel more open. A floating vanity or one with exposed floor beneath it can create the impression of more square footage. Large-format tile can reduce grout lines and make surfaces feel calmer. If possible, keep storage integrated and avoid overfilling the room with bulky fixtures. Small bathrooms also benefit from a clean layout and careful fixture sizing so that each element feels intentional rather than cramped.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small primary bathroom can feel larger with a glass shower enclosure, lighter finishes, a larger mirror, improved lighting, wall-mounted or floating vanity design, and reduced visual clutter. Keeping the floor visible and using large-format tile can also make the room feel more open.
